title: Code of conduct update, arts funding and Kitchener vacancy
subtitle: Bridge rehabilitation tender, $65 million debenture, 2026 calendar deferral, encampment cooling requests and an OLT appeal withdrawal.
overview: Regional Council approved an updated Code of Conduct and Council-staff relations policy {{vote:m23}}, with changes to staff-referral wording, a once-per-term policy review and the rules on access to confidential information. It also declared the Regional Councillor seat for Kitchener, formerly held by Kari Williams, vacant {{vote:m28}}. Council chose to fill it by call for applications, with a special meeting to hear applicants on August 14, 2025 {{vote:m29}}.

Council backed seeking an independent community partner to run the Arts Funding program under a three-year contract {{vote:m9}}, after artists asked for a community-led arts council. It also accepted a tender for rehabilitating the West Montrose Covered Bridge and raised the project budget {{vote:m14}}, and passed by-laws for debenture borrowing totalling $65,000,000 for capital works {{vote:m6}}.

Council withdrew the Region's appeal of a Kitchener zoning by-law amendment to the Ontario Land Tribunal {{vote:m20}}, a matter considered in closed session. It deferred the 2026 meeting calendar to an August 12 special meeting {{vote:m27}}. Delegates also raised cooling access at the 100 Victoria Street encampment, and staff will circulate information to Council.

decisions.item: Code of Conduct and Council-staff relations policy
decisions.detail: Council approved the updated Code of Conduct and Council-staff relations policy with amendments, including removing the 'essential matters' wording, a once-per-term review, and new wording on access to confidential information.
Council approved seeking an independent community partner to manage the Arts Funding program through a three-year contract, in response to the KPMG review.
Council selected appointment by call for applications to fill the vacant Regional Councillor – Kitchener seat, with the selection meeting set for August 14, 2025.
Council accepted the Looby Builders (Dublin) Limited tender of $9,735,297 plus taxes and increased the overall project budget by $4,601,800.
Council withdrew the Region's Ontario Land Tribunal appeal of Kitchener's Zoning By-law Amendment 2025-049.
Council passed the by-law issuing one series of instalment debentures totalling $65,000,000 covering Cambridge, Kitchener, Woolwich and Regional capital works.
Council endorsed the Waterloo Region Immigration Strategy 2025-2028 and committed to advocate for federal and provincial policy and investment.
Council deferred the 2026 meeting calendar, including a proposal to move committee meetings from Tuesdays to Wednesdays, to the August 12, 2025 special meeting.

debate: Arts delegates said artists were not consulted in the KPMG review or on this item and that the agenda item was added late. They asked for an artist-led arts council, with interim funding in the meantime. Several councillors agreed on getting money to artists quickly and supported staff's contract approach.

Staff said the community foundation that ran the fund in 2024 could not continue, so an external partner would be procured. They said a jury of working artists would decide grants and that internal administration would cost about the same. Staff had not found interest from area municipalities. A councillor asked about delegating the grants to area municipalities; others said that would add complexity.

On the 2026 calendar, one councillor asked to move Tuesday committee meetings to Wednesdays to avoid a Cambridge Council clash. Others cited existing commitments, part-time councillors' jobs and the Wellesley schedule. Council deferred the question so Cambridge could look at its own calendar.

On filling the Kitchener vacancy, a delegate proposed a randomly selected citizens' panel. Council noted the time limit in the Municipal Act and the delegate said such a panel might not meet it. Councillors then debated dates for the applicant meeting and moved it to August 14.

Delegates asked for a cooling site at the 100 Victoria Street encampment, citing barriers at other sites. Council asked staff to look at options and post information on cooling and water access, and the commissioner agreed to circulate an update.
